site.title: Yose Rakugo
site.tagline: A rakugo theatre in Asakusa: five storytellers every night.

posts.title: Kiku becomes shin’uchi in spring
posts.excerpt: After eleven years, Sanyutei Kiku will close the bill as a full master from March.
posts.content:
The association announced it on Monday: Sanyutei Kiku, who opened our bill as a zenza in 2015, becomes shin’uchi next spring.

Her promotion run is ten nights here in March. She will close each night with a different story she has never told on our stage.

posts.title: Ghost stories by lantern
posts.excerpt: Every Sunday in October the last story is told with the house lights off.
posts.content:
October is kaidan month. On Sundays at 20:00 the hall goes dark except for the lantern beside the stage.

Shunputei Momo tells Botan-dōrō, the peony lantern, in three parts across the month.

posts.title: What the fan becomes
posts.excerpt: A storyteller has two props. Here is what they turn into.
posts.content:
The folded fan is chopsticks for soba, a pipe, a brush, a sword, an oar. Opened halfway it is a sake cup.

The tenugui towel is a wallet, a letter, a book or a tobacco pouch. Watch the hands: that is where the story is.

posts.title: Your first night at a yose
posts.excerpt: Come in whenever you like, sit anywhere, laugh out loud.
posts.content:
You can walk in mid-bill; the door staff will wait for the end of a story. Shoes off at the top of the stairs.

The first storyteller is an apprentice; the last is the headliner. In between, someone may juggle or cut paper.
